steps.title: In the ground
steps.text: Zirconium is mined as zircon (zirconium silicate), a hard, heavy grain found in the same beach and dune sands as the titanium minerals. Zircon always carries a little hafnium, zirconium's chemical twin: about one part to fifty.

steps.title: Mine and sort
steps.text: Zircon is a co-product of mineral-sands mining. Spirals separate the heavy grains from quartz; magnets and electrostatic plates then split zircon from ilmenite, rutile and monazite.
steps.india: IREL and KMML recover zircon from beach sands, but India imports most of what it uses (about 95,000 t in 2021-22).

steps.title: Mill
steps.text: Most zircon is used as the mineral, with no chemistry at all: ground to a fine white flour that makes ceramic tiles and sanitaryware opaque, or used as sand for foundry moulds and furnace linings.

steps.title: Crack
steps.text: For chemicals and metal, zircon must be broken open: fused with caustic soda, or reacted with chlorine and coke. This gives zirconium oxychloride and tetrachloride, the starting points for zirconia and zirconium chemicals.

steps.title: Separate hafnium
steps.text: Reactor fuel tubes must let neutrons pass. Zirconium does; hafnium absorbs them. So nuclear-grade zirconium has the hafnium stripped out by solvent extraction, down to a few parts in ten thousand, in France, the United States, Russia and China.
out: Hafnium, the only source of it
steps.india: The Nuclear Fuel Complex runs the full chain: about 1,140 t of nuclear-grade oxide in 2021-22.

steps.title: Make metal
steps.text: Purified tetrachloride is reduced with molten magnesium into zirconium sponge, as titanium is. The sponge is melted and alloyed with a little tin, iron and chromium into Zircaloy, then drawn into thin-walled tubes.
steps.india: NFC makes Zircaloy tubes for India's reactors.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Ceramics take the most zircon, then foundries and refractories. Zirconia goes into dental crowns, oxygen sensors and thermal coatings. The metal clads nuclear fuel and lines chemical vessels.
steps.india: The ceramics industry and the Department of Atomic Energy's reactors.
